- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2.0% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term peak; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% below true peak observed in 3–5 day window.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model underestimates true volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.7% to account for sentiment-driven noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–1.5% in 10–15 day window; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to 30d forecast if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to recognize momentum; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast for next 5–7 days.
